newsitem.title: USA: ABC Rail plant upgrades near completion.
newsitem.headline: ABC Rail plant upgrades near completion.

text.p: ABC Rail Products Corp said Wednesday it is nearing completion of a series of strategic plant upgrade, adding it believes it is positioned to capitalize on anticipated orders from the nation's large, or Class I, railroads.

"We have completed improvements at two of our track products plants and expect to complete work at the other two during the second quarter," Chairman Donald Grinter said in a statement. "In addition, we are upgrading our foundry processes at the Calera (Alabama) wheel-manufacturing facility."
Earlier, ABC reported a decline in earnings for the first quarter ended October 31 of $0.06 a share, down from $0.27 a year ago. Sales dropped to $55.9 million from $58.6 million.
The company said it had projected lower results for the first quarter last month.

"The comparatively lower sales and profit during what has historically been one of our slower quarters anyway was the result of softer order levels from our major customers and our decision to accelerate much-needed improvements to our key manufacturing facilities," Grinter said.

He said comparatively lower sales and earnings during what is historically a slower quarter was the result of softer order levels from a major customer, as well as the decision to accelerate improvements to key manufacturing facilities.

"We decided to step up our upgrade efforts during the normal seasonal lull in order to be able to take advantage of our improved capabilities once the market becomes more robust," Grinter said. "Our improvements at the track products facilities are expected to significantly cut lead times and costs and allow us to focus on growing these core businesses."
Grinter said moving up completion of the improvements reduced output at the facilities. Because of relatively fixed costs, the impact of lower sales hurt profitabilty directly.
As of October 31, debt to total capitalization stood at 47 percent, compared with 45 percent as of July 31. Total assets reached $178.9 million compared with $170.1 million.
